rationale:
The answer gets a few things right. It says that in a mixed umbrella the ETF sub-fund is identified rather than the whole umbrella. It also says non-ETF siblings and unlisted classes should not be labelled ETFs. But it misses or contradicts the central requested mechanism.

(1) It never says that Irish rules require the 'UCITS ETF' identifier in the name, constitution, prospectus, KID/KIID and marketing materials (Reg. 88(1)).

(2) It wrongly says that for a sub-fund with listed and unlisted classes, the identifier 'applies to the listed class, not the whole sub-fund'. In fact it may be applied at either sub-fund level or listed-class level, provided the classes are clearly distinguished (Reg. 88(2); CBI Q&A 1016/1088).

(3) Its caveat that 'UCITS ETF is a market term, not a separate UCITS legal category' contradicts the mandatory regulatory identifier requirement.

(4) It replaces the requested identifier usage with LEI, ISIN and ticker identification, which is not the requested mechanism.

(5) It does not mention that class-level identification was already permitted in the pre-2026 Q&A, though it also does not claim this was new in 2026.
